skeleton:
Shakshuka

Libyan · Easy · Serves 3–4

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
Shakshuka — eggs poached in a spiced pepper-tomato pan — is the Sephardic canon's most traveled child: born in the Ottoman Maghreb, carried to Libya and Tunisia and then to Tel Aviv's cafés and from there to the world's brunch menus, and claimed by every kitchen it passed through. The #22 wrap on this site is its street format; this master record carries the full pan: the pepper-tomato base cooked down properly, the eggs poached at its surface, the bread for the sopping, and the whole family's quiet argument about whether peppers, onions, or both run the base.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

Ingredients

- **Cook the base down — the pan is a sauce, not a soup.** The shakshuka's most common failure abroad is the wet pan: the pepper-onion-tomato must reduce until a spoon's trail holds and the oil's red-gold separates at the edges, because the eggs poach in the sauce's body, not swim in its broth. - **The bridge:** none needed — the whole row is the daily shelf. The family's dial: the Libyan school runs the peppers dominant; the Tunisian runs more onion and the harissa's fire; the modern café runs the feta's cream. All are honest seats at the pan's table.

Doneness & Quality Checkpoints

  • The base: reduced to the spoon's trail, the oil's red-gold at the edges.
  • The eggs: 4–5 minutes covered, molten yolks, the first-set pull.
  • The service: the pan to the table, the bread the plate.

Shakshuka

Prep: 15 minutes · Cook: 30 minutes · Total: About 45 minutes · Serves 3–4

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 4 tbsp olive oil (about 50 g); 2 onions (about 300 g), sliced
  • 3 peppers, red and green mixed (about 350 g), sliced in ribbons
  • 5 cloves garlic (about 20 g), sliced; 1 tsp cumin; ½ tsp sweet paprika; ¼ tsp chile flakes or 1 tsp harissa (#91)
  • 800 g tomatoes, grated, or 1 large can crushed; 1 tsp salt; a pinch of sugar (about 2 g)
  • 5 eggs (about 250 g); a fist of cilantro or parsley (about 15 g)
  • Bread (about 300 g) for the table; the #104 pickled turnips or a sharp salad beside; feta or #92 preserved lemon threads, the modern dials

Instructions

  1. **The base's slow down (20 minutes).** Warm the oil; soften the onions 5 minutes; the peppers in with the garlic and the spices, covered, 8 minutes until wilted and glossy; the tomatoes, the salt, and the sugar — uncovered now, and simmering 10 to 12 minutes more, stirring occasionally, until the pan's sauce is thick, the spoon's trail holds, and the oil's red-gold runs at the edges. Checkpoint — the base's test: a spoon drawn through the pan's center leaves a trail that closes slowly — the sauce's body built. Taste: sweet pepper and tomato's jam, cumin's warmth, the garlic's rounded depth — one notch past salted (the eggs will calm).
  2. **The eggs' poach (4–5 minutes uncovered).** Make five wells in the sauce's surface with the spoon's back; crack an egg into each. Cover the pan, and cook 4–5 minutes — the whites set to just-opaque, the yolks still molten — pulling the pan off the flame at the first set (the carryover finishes while the pan travels). Checkpoint — the eggs' law: the yolk must run at the table's first break — a set yolk is a failed shakshuka, and the 4-minute window (the covered pan's barely-shivering 85–95 °C surface) is the whole clock. The whites' edges should just turn from glassy.
  3. **The finish and the bread's ceremony.** The herbs scattered over, the pan to the table's center with the bread beside — each diner breaking bread, scooping egg and sauce together, the pan's expanse the shared plate. Checkpoint — eating test: the bread's crack or chew, the sauce's sweet-spice depth, and the yolk's gold breaking into the pan's red — each scoop carrying egg's richness and the base's jam — the herbs' green and the pickle's cut (or the feta's salt) between the bites. It should taste like the family's whole argument settled at the pan: the base's patience, the eggs' mercy of minutes, and the bread that makes the pan the plate.

Finish & Plate

The pan itself to the table's center on its trivet — the eggs' gold in the sauce's red, the herbs' green over — the bread at every hand, the pickles or feta beside, and the shared pan the service's oldest argument.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Pan soupy, eggs swamBase under-reducedThe trail-holds test before the eggs
Yolks set hardOver-covered or heldThe 4-minute pull; the pan travels
Base one-note sweetSpices or garlic shyThe cumin leads; the garlic rounds

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- The base keeps 3 days refrigerated and improves (the shakshuka station — the eggs always poached at the pan's reheat); the built pan waits no one. The #22 wrap is the street format's own record. - Variations: the merguez-added ojja register, the green-sauce spring cousin, the feta's modern crumble. This master record is the family's home; the block's #33 and #86 are its other seats.
